head: 4639f55b3

boundaries: the 403 body the fetch client parses
the error every lib/api caller receives
the hub page's redirect and retry

notes: The fetch client keeps the whole body; the hub page reads a private hub from it. One pass, no finding; one redundant condition removed.

instruments.evidence: c892778e1..(this ledger): 3b1422f7b (lib/api throws apiRequestError from one builder for request and upload, with the parsed body on it), 43e507d18 (HubPage decides a private hub with isPrivateHubRefusal for both the redirect and the retry; message matching, dead Axios reads and a debug log gone), 9f8ff2a14 (ModMailModal's dead Axios read gone), and the review's simplification to access_required alone. Boundaries: the 403 body the fetch client parses, the error every lib/api caller receives, the hub page's redirect and retry.
Read c8b7746de (the two pages fixed for lib/api's error shape; it named HubPage's dead reads as out of scope) and de7bcbe8b (the C7 miss that started this: a hand-built Axios error in a test).

The private hub screen is rendered in tests from an error built by the client's own builder; not rendered in the pane, because DERRF is a site admin and opens every hub, and signing the pane out would end the user's session.

Printed the server's real answer in the pane: GET /hubs/privatetest/posts without the session cookie answers 403 {access_required: true, error: 'This hub is private and you do not have access', hub_name, hub_title, privacy_type: 'private'} -- no message and no code field; the client's message falls back to error. With the session (an admin) every one of the 47 hubs answers 200.
access_required is the same key on the server (hubs.go) and in isPrivateHubRefusal.
The page reads status and body.access_required, the fields apiRequestError sets from the real response.
ApiError gained an index signature, so the parsed body's extra fields are typed as unknown and read explicitly.
C10 below breaks the reader (the access_required check, the retry rule) and the tests fail.
The hub page test builds its error with apiRequestError, the builder the client itself uses; the client test runs the real client on the server's real body shape (B3).
A private hub's 403 opens the private hub screen whatever the message says.
A 403 without access_required does not redirect unless the hub's settings say private (the unchanged fallback).
Sibling throw site: uploadFile built its own error without status or code; it now uses the same builder.
isPrivateHubRefusal's true and false outcomes are both reached (the private tests and every other hub test).
The retry no longer hides a private hub's answer for three attempts.
Two throw sites became one builder; two private-hub checks (retry and redirect) became one rule; the review removed a second, redundant condition inside it.

Every reader of access_required or of a private hub's message in the frontend: only HubPage (grep). Every Axios-shape read left: refusals.ts and hubAIDesignerService, both on the axios client, which is right for them.

instruments.why: No finding; the fixes were each run against their pre-fix code (the hub page test fails on the old page).

instruments.evidence: tsc -b and eslint clean on every changed file.
The server's real answer was printed (B3). The redirect was not seen in a browser: the only account signed in is a site admin that opens every hub; said to the user.

instruments.why: Nothing starts before the decision that governs it.
No Go test in this change.

instruments.evidence: The user asked me to look at the Axios-shape reads in HubPage: the page now reads the server's signal, and the client keeps it.
Ran every test file that imports or mocks lib/api, uploadFile, BugReportModal or HubPage: 32 files, 253 passed; the mod mail tests pass.

instruments.why: No earlier control targets lib/api.ts, HubPage.tsx or ModMailModal.tsx.

instruments.evidence: The client test runs the real client with only the transport faked.
The new tests share no mutable state; HubPage.test's private cases clear the posts mock first.
Producers of the error the page reads: lib/api's one builder, for both request and upload. Producer of access_required: one handler.

Removed each new line: the access_required check, the retry rule, the body on the error, the upload builder -- each fails a test. Found one line no test could notice (privacy_type as a second signal the real body always pairs with access_required) and removed it rather than test a body the server never sends.
The private hub tests wait for the private screen before counting requests.

gates.lint: eslint clean on the changed files
gates.tests: 32 files using lib/api, 253 passed; HubPage 7; client errors 2; mod mail 2.
